title: Evidence Dispatcher Operational Spec & SIEM Compatibility Matrix
body:
Purpose
This doc defines the operational spec for the Evidence Dispatcher (a.k.a. dispatch-orch), the adaptive routing layer that receives normalized control-evidence envelopes from collectors and routes them to downstream sinks (SIEM exports, archive, forensic indexer, and long-term cold storage). It includes: compatibility requirements for common SIEMs, envelope guarantees, routing and dedup behavior, credential rotation considerations, and a pragmatic rollout checklist.

Scope
- In-scope: routing logic and adapter contracts for SIEMs (Splunk, SumoLogic, Datadog, Elastic via Logstash), envelope validation, priority-based queueing, redrive semantics, idempotency and dedup, minimal enrichment (tags, provenance), and operational monitoring.
- Out-of-scope: collector-side capture logic (assume collectors produce normalized envelope), deep forensic indexing (handled by forensic-indexer service), and UI/console UX.

Goals
- Ensure every control-evidence envelope reaches at least one compliant sink within SLOs.
- Prevent duplicate evidence ingestion into SIEM and archive for regulatory accuracy.
- Provide clear compatibility mappings and example transforms for major SIEMs.
- Keep operational complexity low: simple fallback policies, clear observability.

High-level flow
1) Collector -> Evidence Ingest API (normalizes, signs, timestamps).
2) Ingest -> Dispatcher queue (kafka/topic partitioned by org_id and evidence_type).
3) Dispatcher consumers pick messages, validate envelope, enrich metadata, consult routing policy, and call adapters.
4) Adapter returns success/failure/status-with-retry-window.
5) Dispatcher emits audit events to the audit-log topic and updates delivery state in the delivery-store.

Envelope contract (required fields)
- envelope_id: string (uuid v4)
- org_id: string
- evidence_type: string (control-run, access-audit, attestation)
- created_at: rfc3339 timestamp (collector)
- captured_at: rfc3339 timestamp (source)
- provenance: list of short strings (collector-id, host, process)
- payload_ref: s3/gcs/http+signed url OR inline base64 (prefer ref for large artifacts)
- payload_schema: short string identifier (e.g., audit.v2.access)
- signature: base64 (collector signing key id should be in provenance)
- delivery_preferences: optional object (priority: high|normal|low; sinks: [siem,archive,forensic])

Note: currently collectors produce a minimal delivery_preferences. Dispatcher enriches with org-level policies.

Delivery guarantees and dedup
- At-least-once to primary sink(s). To avoid duplicates we use two mechanisms: stable dedup-key and sink-acknowledged offsets.
- Dedup-key construction: sha256(envelope_id || payload_sha256 || org_id). Stored in delivery-store with ttl=90d. If seen, Dispatcher marks as duplicate and emits a duplicate_audit event.
- If a sink is non-idempotent (some legacy SIEM endpoints), Dispatcher will attempt single delivery and, on ambiguous outcome, mark for manual review.

Routing policies and fallback
- Per-org routing config (stored in config-store): preferred_sinks ordered, priority thresholds, region preferences, and compliance flags (jurisdictional hold).
- Default policy: [siem, archive]. For high-priority evidence (priority=high) try primary SIEM, then fallback to forensic-indexer in the same region, then cross-region archive if allowed.
- Failure modes: transient network failures -> exponential backoff with jitter, up to 5 attempts within 30 minutes. Persistent failure -> escalate to human queue and emit pager alert if evidence priority=high.

SIEM adapter compatibility matrix (summary)
- Splunk HTTP Event Collector (HEC): supports JSON + index-time fields; prefer envelope transformed to {time, host, sourcetype, event} with event containing minimal envelope metadata. 
- Elastic (Logstash/Beats): send as JSON doc; ensure payload_schema maps to a typed index pattern. Use ingest pipelines for parsing payloads.
- Datadog Log API: envelope must be mapped to attributes + tags; length limits on message -> use payload_ref rather than inline payload for large artifacts.
- SumoLogic: supports JSON or key-value pairs; prefer JSON with _sourceCategory set to org_id/evidence_type.

Compatibility quirks and transforms
- Timestamp handling: many SIEMs expect epoch_millis or ISO8601; adapter must supply both if possible.
- Field name collisions: envelope.metadata fields should be prefixed with rd_ (e.g., rd_envelope_id, rd_org_id) to avoid collision with customer log fields.
- Binary payloads: never inline binaries into SIEM events. Put payload_ref and a short preview/thumbnail text in the event.

Sample transform (pseudo-JSON shown for operator clarity)
{
  "time": "<captured_at>",
  "host": "collector-12.redwood.internal",
  "sourcetype": "rd_evidence:audit.v2.access",
  "event": {
    "rd_envelope_id": "<envelope_id>",
    "rd_org_id": "<org>",
    "action": "user.login",
    "user": "alice@example.com",
    "payload_ref": "s3://evidence-bucket/...",
    "rd_provenance": ["collector-12","service-a"]
  }
}

Credential rotation and auth model
- Dispatcher -> SIEM adapters authenticate via per-org credentials stored in secrets-manager. Keys must rotate every 90 days. Adapters support two active keys (current, previous) to avoid in-flight failures during rollout.
- For SIEMs with webhook-style endpoints, we sign outbound requests with a dispatcher-service key and include X-RD-Signature header. SIEM customers may require whitelisting dispatcher IP ranges.

Operational monitoring and SLOs
- Delivery latency SLO: 95th percentile to primary SIEM < 60s for normal priority, < 10s for high priority (best-effort).
- Success rate: >= 99% for primary deliveries across all orgs (30d window).
- Metrics emitted: deliveries_total, deliveries_success, deliveries_failed, deliveries_dup_detected, adapter_latencies, redrive_count. Traces: per-envelope trace id propagated to all downstream systems.

Observability and debugging playbook
- If deliveries_failed spikes: check adapter health, credentials expiry, network ACLs to SIEM, and per-org routing overrides.
- For duplicates: consult delivery-store TTL and dedup-key collisions, check whether collector re-emitted due to local retries.
- For schema mismatches: adapter emits schema_error with sample payload_ref; open a ticket to collector team to patch.

Redrive and manual review flows
- Redrive API will accept envelope_id and target sinks. Redrive marks a new dispatch attempt with a new dispatch_id, links to original envelope.
- Manual review UI (ops) should present payload preview (first 2KB), provenance chain, delivery logs, and quick actions: retry, escalate, mark_ignored.

Testing and rollout checklist
- Unit tests for adapter transforms and timestamp handling.
- Integration tests: end-to-end from ingest -> dispatcher -> mock SIEM (splunk mock endpoint, elastic test cluster).
- Chaos tests: simulate SIEM outage and verify fallback to archive and escalation.
- Canary rollout: 5% traffic for 48h, watch deliveries_success and adapter_latencies.
- Gradual ramp with automated kill switch if p95 latency or error rate exceeds threshold.

Open questions / decisions to make
- Per-org retention for delivery-store: 90d default, is 365d required for legal hold customers? (legal to weigh in)
- Standardized tagset for regulatory classification (rd_class: pci,hipaa,gdpr) — should dispatcher normalize or collectors supply?
- Can we enforce a single canonical timestamp (captured_at vs created_at) for SIEM events or leave both?

TODOs
- [ ] Add Splunk HEC sample request with token rotation example. (owner: Tom)
- [ ] Finalize dedup-key TTL policy with Legal. (owner: Asha)
- [ ] Implement adapter tests for Datadog limits. (owner: Diego)

Appendix: quick RFC links
- Confluence: evidence-pipeline-overview (linked_artifacts above)
- Design note: delivery-store-indexing-strategy (will link once available)
- GitHub: evidence-dispatcher prototype (linked_artifacts above)

Notes to reviewers
- This is an operational-first doc — expect rough edges. Please call out any SIEM compatibility behaviors you rely on or special-casing required by enterprise customers. Also flag any regulatory constraints (jurisdictional hold, e-discovery) that should alter routing.

End of spec
